decision_reason: NASA's KSC-14109 catalog record identifies the HLA2MPC 3.0 bridge and links this public repository; the source has three subcomponents and a LICENSE.pdf. However, I could not verify the text/version of that PDF grant from the available repository view, and the repository has no published GitHub release or practical setup/use guide. The NASA catalog supplies a functional description but not installation guidance. Hold pending exact grant text/version and release/user guidance; do not treat the repository's NASA location or metadata labels as sufficient.

eligible_license.note: The repository contains LICENSE.pdf and NASA classifies KSC-14109 as Open Source, but the actual PDF grant text/version was not readable in this review environment. Confirm exact OSI-approved license and that it covers the assigned software before admission.

decision_reason: NASA's current GSC-18917-1 record identifies cFS Data Storage application v2.6.0, labels it Open Source, and links directly to this repository. The public source is an independently installable/reusable cFS application with an application user's guide and NASA mission-science documentation of the exact DS role. The current repository has an Apache-2.0 grant and substantive source changes in 2026. NASA's March 2015 open-source release announcement identifies Data Storage v2.0 as an individual application released to the public, which is the earliest defensible product-source year; the current GitHub root Apache license itself was added in 2020. This is the DS app component, not the entire cFS framework.

government_provenance.note: NASA's current catalog identifies the exact cFS Data Storage application, release v2.6.0, and links to the assigned nasa/DS repository. NASA's GSFC cFS material identifies the framework/application suite as developed at Goddard.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the C Data Storage flight-software application, user-guide source/build instructions, configuration and test material without credentials; the dev branch has substantive changes through September 2026.

eligible_license.note: The exact current root LICENSE is Apache License 2.0. It was added in https://github.com/nasa/DS/commit/561c79c3fcc6381fc7fcfc8afdf9c21490b35495 (2020-08-18); NASA's current GSC-18917-1 item is also classified Open Source. NASA's earlier v2.0 catalog/SourceForge distribution is noted separately for source chronology and should not be treated as extending the current root Apache grant to other cFS modules.

primary_evidence.note: NASA currently publishes version 2.6.0 as an open-source download and describes its spacecraft onboard storage role. The repository includes application-specific user-guide source and documentation. NASA's 2024 DAVINCI Data Prioritization paper documents use of the exact heritage Data Storage (DS) application for onboard operational-data files: https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20240002486/downloads/IPPW2024%2025.pdf.

product_identity: Core Flight System (cFS) Data Storage application (DS), version 2.6.0: a reusable flight-software app that stores software-bus messages and other onboard data in files for later ground transmission
agency: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Core Flight System team
geography: United States federal spacecraft and flight-software engineering; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Greenbelt, Maryland
license: Apache-2.0 for the current nasa/DS repository code; the earlier 2015 SourceForge v2.0 package was separately cataloged by NASA as Open Source and retains its own historical license scope
status_note: Active: exact repository has substantive 2026 source changes and a current NASA v2.6.0 open-source distribution. NASA's March 2015 release announcement names the v2.0 DS app as one of the released cFS applications and the original GSC-16126-1 catalog record linked its source archive, establishing the earliest public code year. The current GitHub Apache LICENSE first appears in 2020; the 2015 release is an earlier project-level public source milestone, not a claim that today's Apache file existed then. Product-family note: this is one standalone cFS application, not the cFS framework or whole application suite.

decision_reason: NASA's MFS-33274-1 Software Catalog page labels DualPol Open Source and links directly to this public repository. The exact LICENSE.md is NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3, identifies the same software designation/title and Marshall Space Flight Center, and grants worldwide use, distribution, modification and redistribution. The 2015 functional package and grant are verifiable. README contains an install command, dependencies, import examples, and a demonstration notebook; NASA technical reports document DualPol's specific precipitation-retrieval application. NASA's live catalog direct distribution supports the stable-source exception, but the README's tested Python versions are old and this should not be called actively developed.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact MFS-33274-1 record identifies the Python Interface to Dual-Pol Radar Algorithms and links to the assigned repository. LICENSE.md names NASA Marshall Space Flight Center, MFS-33274-1, and the same title; NASA MSFC publications describe the research product.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Python radar-retrieval package, setup.py, notebooks, README, and change log without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The exact file is NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 (NASA-1.3), names MFS-33274-1/DualPol and Marshall Space Flight Center, and grants worldwide software rights; NASA-1.3 is OSI approved (https://opensource.org/license/NASA-1.3). The first grant-bearing public source history is https://github.com/nasa/DualPol/commit/85a2fb3dd25472eef0beabe74b9eaf991225e5e1 (2015-07-01). Requested recipient registration is not a condition of the license grant.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's MSFC technical paper explicitly identifies the exact DualPol software and describes its integration with DOE ARM Py-ART and CSU_RadarTools for precipitation-characteristic retrievals. The NASA catalog continues to distribute this named module, and README gives installation, import, dependency, and demo-notebook guidance.

product_identity: DualPol 1.0.2, an object-oriented Python package/interface for polarimetric radar precipitation retrievals, hydrometeor identification, rain rate, particle-size distribution, and water/ice estimates
agency: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Earth Science Branch
geography: United States federal Earth-science and weather-radar research; NASA Marshall Space Flight Center, Huntsville, Alabama
license: NASA Open Source Agreement v1.3 (NASA-1.3) for the DualPol repository's own source; dependencies Py-ART, CSU_RadarTools, SkewT and scientific Python packages remain under their own licenses
status_note: Maintained distribution exception: NASA's current MFS-33274-1 record still offers the exact source. This is a small scientific Python module with documented retrieval use and install guidance, not a standalone radar processing suite; do not include or relicense its external Py-ART/CSU dependencies. README documents legacy Python 2.7/3.4–3.6 support, so catalog as Maintained (stable/distributed), not Active.

decision_reason: NASA's LEW-19264-1 catalog page identifies EADIN as C++ microcontroller communication-protocol software, links directly to this source, and accurately limits it to demonstration/testing rather than flight-certified use. The repository has an Apache-2.0 grant, a user manual, protocol details and measured deployment examples. A NASA Glenn hardware-in-the-loop paper documents the exact EADIN Lite protocol in a network-in-the-loop simulation with C-MAPSS40k; that exact scientific use plus the official NASA product distribution meets notability. First grant-bearing functional source is 2016.

government_provenance.note: NASA's exact LEW-19264-1 catalog page identifies the EADIN Communication Protocol and directly links this repository. README names its NASA Glenn Research Center Intelligent Control and Autonomy Branch author and says it supported the Fixed Wing Aeronautics distributed-engine-control task.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes C++ protocol implementation, example code, README, License.txt, and a User_Manual.docx without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The exact repository License.txt applies Apache License 2.0. License was publicly added in https://github.com/nasa/EADINLite/commit/c90840583d7279527dd19977b13fb20d096d1590 (2016-02-24); functional source was already present in the public tree.

primary_evidence.note: The exact NASA Glenn conference paper identifies the Engine Area Distributed Interconnect Network Lite (EADIN Lite) as the real-time protocol in a network-in-the-loop simulation integrated with C-MAPSS40k. NASA's current LEW-19264-1 page confirms this source is a demonstration/testing protocol, not mission-certified software. README includes successful Arduino deployments and measured timing/memory behavior; the manual provides user guidance.

product_identity: EADIN Lite, a C++ implementation and example of the Engine Area Distributed Interconnect Network protocol for deterministic communication among microcontrollers in distributed engine-control test/simulation networks
agency: NASA Glenn Research Center, Intelligent Control and Autonomy Branch; developed for the Fixed Wing Aeronautics distributed-engine-control research task
geography: United States federal aeronautics and propulsion research; NASA Glenn Research Center, Cleveland, Ohio
license: Apache-2.0 for EADINLite repository source; microcontroller platform, network hardware, C-MAPSS40k, and other applications are outside the grant
status_note: Maintained distribution exception: NASA's current LEW-19264-1 catalog record directly links the exact repository even though source activity is quiet. This is research/demo software only; NASA explicitly states it is not mission-certified and used for demonstration/testing. The 2017 NASA Glenn paper documents use of the exact protocol in HIL simulation; do not suggest flight readiness.

decision_reason: This was an Apache-2.0 Flask API that NASA exposed on api.nasa.gov for Landsat 8 imagery and that README says was used in demos/integrations. The exact README now says the project is archived and the service has been replaced by Earthdata GIBS; it also states the code was originally developed by others. Hold rather than admit as a current NASA service: current exact deployment/source parity is absent, and the available evidence does not yet establish the unusually significant historical status needed for a new Archived catalog record.

government_provenance.note: README says this exact Flask API was provided to the public through api.nasa.gov and existed there for several years; that establishes NASA service operation/stewardship, although README also says it was originally developed by others, so this is not a NASA-authorship claim.

public_source.note: The repository publicly exposes the Flask API, deployment files, docs and Apache license.

eligible_license.note: The exact root LICENSE is Apache 2.0 for the source repository; it does not grant rights to Google Earth Engine or its imagery/data.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party README explicitly says the service was replaced by Earthdata GIBS and the project is archived. No current NASA deployment/distribution of this exact API source was verified, and the README's qualitative claim of prior demos/integrations is not enough by itself to establish unusually significant historical relevance.

product_identity: Historic NASA Earth Imagery API Flask service for simple Landsat 8 imagery queries; not the successor Earthdata GIBS service
agency: NASA API program / NASA public APIs service (README says source was originally developed by others; NASA role verified only as service operator/steward)
geography: United States federal Earth-observation API; NASA public-data service
license: Apache-2.0 for this repository's code; Google Earth Engine and imagery/data rights are separate
